articles.title: Optimum Communications, Fluence Energy, Virgin Galactic And Other Big Stocks Moving Higher Today
articles.teaser: Several stocks, including Optimum Communications Services, surged while Dow fell. Technology, energy, and aerospace stocks saw notable gains.
articles.body:
U.S. stocks traded lower during today's session, with the Dow falling more than 65 points on Monday. However, several technology, energy, and aerospace stocks posted notable gains.

Shares of Optimum Communications Services Inc. (NYSE:OPTU) rose sharply to lead the list of top percentage gainers.  The company announced a tender offer to buy back up to 120 million of its shares at $2.50 per share.

The buyback represents about 42.5% of the issued and outstanding shares of Class A Common Stock as of May 27, 2026. The tender offer will expire at 5:00 pm (ET) on June 30, 2026.

Optimum Communications Services surged 93.71% to $1.27 on Monday.

Here are some other big stocks recording gains in today’s session.

  • Fluence Energy, Inc. (NASDAQ:FLNC) jumped 34.58% to $25.41.
  • Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:SPCE) gained 28.80% to $7.96, continuing the strong upward momentum from late last week. Stock market traders are rapidly accumulating positions in the space tourism pioneer, driven by several high-profile catalysts.
  • The Elmet Group Holdings Limited (NASDAQ:ELMT) climbed 25.0% to $19.10. The company reported strong first quarter earnings, with revenue up 20.7% to $56 million.
  • Taylor Morrison Home Corporation (NYSE:TMHC) advanced 22.46% to $71.64, following the announcement that Berkshire Hathaway has agreed to acquire the company in a $6.8 billion deal.
  • Edgewise Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:EWTX) rose 14.72% to $39.19, after the company announced the sale of its muscular dystrophy business to Servier for $2.65 billion.
  • Arm Holdings plc (NASDAQ:ARM) gained 13.63% to $401.47, after Nvidia unveiled its new RTX Spark chip, based on Arm Holdings' designs.
  • Replimune Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:REPL) climbed 13.0% to $9.82. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) prioritized the resubmission of the company's experimental advanced melanoma drug, RP1.
  • AirJoule Technologies Corporation (NASDAQ:AIRJ) advanced 12.9% to $5.07.
  • Asana, Inc. (NYSE:ASAN) rose 12.85% to $8.69.

articles.title: Virgin Galactic Stock Rallies 180% In A Month — Short Sellers Feel The Heat
articles.teaser: Virgin Galactic stock surges over 180% in May to mark its best month ever.
articles.body:
Virgin Galactic Holdings Inc. (NYSE:SPCE) has been one of the most explosive trades of the spring, surging more than 165% over the past month and turning short sellers into reluctant spectators as retail momentum builds ahead of a critical commercial launch window.

  • SPCE stock is racing higher. Watch the price action here. 

The Catalysts

The stock climbed from $2.47 on May 20 to as high as $6.18 by May 29 — a move that played out in nine trading days and caught many bears off guard. 

The catalyst stack driving the rally is real: a successful glide test of VSS Unity on May 27 at Spaceport America, a court settlement clearing a litigation overhang that had hung over the stock since 2022 and a Jefferies analyst reaffirming the company’s Q4 2026 commercial launch roadmap.

The upcoming, highly anticipated SpaceX IPO driving renewed interest in the space sector is the icing on the catalyst cake. 

Read Also: What Is SMCI Stock Worth Without The Scandal Discount?

Short sellers who had been pressing SPCE shares lower on cash burn concerns suddenly found themselves on the wrong side of a momentum trade. 

With retail traders flooding into SPCE on social platforms and volume spikes signaling fresh speculative interest, the squeeze dynamics became self-reinforcing — every uptick forcing more covering, which drove prices higher, which forced more covering.

The Fundamentals

The fundamental picture hasn’t changed dramatically. 

Virgin Galactic remains in a pre-revenue phase, burning roughly $93 million in free cash flow per quarter against a liquidity buffer of approximately $220 to $251 million. 

The company carries a going concern disclosure in its 2025 annual report, and the math on runway is tight — two to three quarters at current burn rates before additional capital would be needed. None of that is new information. What changed is sentiment.

The May 27 glide test was the first actual flight activity in two years, and markets treated it as proof-of-concept for management’s timeline. 

Virgin Galactic has guided Q3 2026 for additional Delta-class glide tests, with rocket-powered flights and a commercial launch targeted for Q4. 

At $750,000 per seat, the company has reopened ticket sales for roughly 50 flights — a backlog that could convert into real revenue if the timeline holds.

The Bottom Line

Whether the short squeeze has more room to run depends on two things: how much short interest remains in the float, and whether the company can string together operational milestones without a slip. 

Any delay in the Delta-class test schedule would give bears an opening to reload. Conversely, each successful test between now and October is likely to trigger another round of covering.

Read Also: Palantir Stock Is Either A Bargain Or A Bubble, Depending On Who You Ask

For now, retail bulls are in control of the tape with SPCE stock up another 25% on Monday morning, per Benzinga Pro. 

Short sellers are not out of the picture — the cash burn story hasn’t gone away — but for the moment, the trade belongs to anyone who believes Virgin Galactic will finally reach orbit on its commercial ambitions.

The next 90 days will tell a lot.

SPCE Price Action: Virgin Galactic Holdings shares were up 25.89% at $7.78 at the time of publication on Monday. The stock is trading at a new 52-week high, according to Benzinga Pro data.

Over the past month, SPCE has gained about 183.9% versus a 5.0% rise in the S&P 500 and is up roughly 127% year-to-date compared to the index’s 10.2% gain.

articles.title: Why Is Virgin Galactic Stock Soaring Monday?
articles.teaser: Virgin Galactic (NYSE: SPCE) stock surges over 23% premarket amid heavy retail momentum, institutional stake disclosure, and SpaceX IPO buzz.
articles.body:
Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc. (NYSE:SPCE) shares are surging on Monday, carrying over significant upward momentum from late last week. Stock market traders are piling into the space tourism pioneer amid a confluence of high-profile catalysts.

Heavy Retail Momentum Drives Surge

The aggressive buying on Monday follows a performance on Friday, when SPCE shares closed up 36.42% at $6.18. Beyond positive operational milestones, traders are exhibiting broader investor enthusiasm, partly fueled by the ongoing SpaceX initial public offering speculation that has captured the attention of the wider market.

Institutional Stake Disclosed

According to a schedule 13G filed on Friday with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Huang Rich and RichRich Capital LLC disclosed a substantial position in the company. As of Thursday Huang may be deemed to beneficially own 5,580,600 shares, representing a 5.26% institutional stake in the outer-space transport firm. The position includes a significant chunk of shares underlying call options.

Legal Settlement Lifts Overhang

The Monday rally also builds on momentum sparked Friday after the company announced a federal court granted preliminary approval of a settlement resolving two longstanding shareholder derivative lawsuits. The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York approved the deal, which mandates a $2.75 million payment from Virgin Galactic’s insurers to the company.

SPCE Technical Levels To Watch This Week

SPCE is trading far above its trend gauges: about 140.4% above the 20-day SMA ($3.08) and 132.6% above the 200-day SMA ($3.18).

RSI is the cleanest momentum read right now, and at 86.78 it’s deep in overbought territory after first entering overbought conditions in May.

Trend structure is mixed under the hood: the 20-day SMA is above the 50-day SMA (bullish near-term alignment), but the death cross from January (50-day SMA below the 200-day SMA) is still a longer-term caution flag.

  • Key Resistance: $7.33 — price is extended above the prior 52-week high ($6.61), so the premarket level itself becomes the immediate air pocket test
  • Key Support: $6.61 — prior 52-week high zone from May that often acts as first support after a breakout

SPCE Stock Price Activity: Virgin Galactic shares were up 23.30% at $7.620 during premarket trading on Monday, according to Benzinga Pro data.

articles.title: Consumer Tech News (May 25-29): Dell, IBM, CrowdStrike, Meta Lead Big Tech AI Push
articles.teaser: Dell beats massive estimates, IBM launches $5B Project Lightwell, CrowdStrike expands cyber insurance AI efforts, and Meta adds paid AI subscriptions across platforms.
articles.body:
Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA) on Thursday criticized the President Donald Trump Administration's decision to introduce a $250 bill featuring a portrait of the President.

Earnings Results

Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL)  reported first-quarter revenue of $43.84 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $35.45 billion, according to Benzinga Pro. Adjusted earnings came in at $4.86 per share, well above expectations of $2.94 per share.

UiPath Inc. (NYSE:PATH) reported quarterly earnings of 15 cents per share, which missed the Street estimate of 16 cents. Revenue clocked in at $418.38 million, which beat the consensus estimate of $397.81 million.

MongoDB Inc (NASDAQ:MDB) posted first-quarter revenue of $687.62 million, beating analyst estimates of $667.82 million and adjusted earnings of $1.32 per share, beating analyst estimates of $1.18 per share.

Autodesk Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) reported earnings of $2.99 per share, which beat the consensus estimate of $2.84. Revenue came in at $1.93 billion, which beat the Street estimate of $1.89 billion.

Weibo Corp. (NASDAQ:WB) reported first-quarter revenue of $421.3 million and above the analyst consensus estimate of $417.9 million.

Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM) reported first-quarter revenue of $11.13 billion, beating the consensus estimate of $11.05 billion and adjusted earnings of $3.88 per share, well above estimates of $3.12 per share.

Li Auto Inc. (NASDAQ:LI) reported first-quarter 2026 revenue of 23.0 billion Chinese yuan ($3.33 billion), but exceeded the analyst consensus estimate of $3.14 billion. Adjusted net loss came in at 2.09 yuan per American depositary share, or 30 cents, compared with Wall Street expectations for a profit of 7 cents per share.

XPeng Inc. (NYSE:XPEV) reported quarterly revenue of 13.03 billion Chinese yuan ($1.89 billion), down 17.6% year over year and below the analyst consensus estimate of $3.13 billion. 

Photronics Inc. (NASDAQ:PLAB) reported non-GAAP net income attributable to shareholders of $24.9 million, or 42 cents per diluted share, missing the estimated 54 cents per share.

Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) reported first-quarter results that narrowly topped Wall Street estimates and issued upbeat long-term growth projections tied to AI infrastructure demand.

HP Inc. (NYSE:HPQ) reported quarterly earnings of 86 cents per share, which beat the consensus of 71 cents and revenue came in at $14.41 billion, which beat the Street estimate of $14.04 billion.

Synopsys Inc. (NASDAQ:SNPS) reported quarterly earnings of $3.35 per share, which beat the Street estimate of $3.15 and revenue of $2.28 billion, which beat the consensus estimate of $2.25 billion.

Marvell Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MRVL) reported earnings of 80 cents per share, which beat the analyst consensus estimate of 79 cents, and revenue came in at $2.42 billion, which beat the analyst consensus estimate of $2.4 billion.

Kingsoft Cloud Holdings Limited (NASDAQ:KC) reported first-quarter fiscal 2026 results, with revenue rising year over year and topping analyst estimates as demand for AI-related cloud services accelerated.

Technology, Hardware & IT

Dell said that some of its biggest AI customers are signing multi-year server deals without knowing the final price, prioritizing access to computing power over cost as demand continues to overwhelm supply.

The Pentagon awarded Dell Federal Systems a five-year, $9.7 billion deal to manage Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) software licensing across the Defense Department, intelligence community and U.S. Coast Guard.

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) and Red Hat launched Project Lightwell, a $5 billion initiative focused on securing open source software as AI-driven cyber threats increase.

Infosys Limited (NYSE:INFY) on Thursday announced a lineup of new AI-powered digital experiences for tennis fans in partnership with Roland-Garros.

Nebius Group N.V. (NASDAQ:NBIS) shares are rising in extended trading on Wednesday after Situational Awareness reported a 5.6% stake in the neocloud company.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWD) is expanding its Project QuiltWorks initiative with major players in the cyber insurance industry.

Super Micro Computer, Inc (NASDAQ:SMCI) is collaborating with Taiwanese authorities to help prevent illicit diversion of its server technology.

Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META) is expanding beyond its advertising roots by introducing paid subscriptions across Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Meta AI as the company looks to unlock new AI-driven revenue streams and deepen monetization of its massive global user base.

CoreWeave, Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV) launched unified agentic AI capabilities aimed at enhancing the development of reliable AI agents.

Semiconductors

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd (NYSE:TSM) Senior Vice President of Business Development Kevin Zhang told Reuters that rising electricity demand from AI is making energy efficiency a central priority for future chip development.

Bloomberg reported that Qualcomm Inc (NASDAQ:QCOM) reached a deal to supply TikTok parent ByteDance with application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) for AI data centers.

Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang announced the company plans to spend approximately $150 billion a year in Taiwan.

IREN Limited (NASDAQ:IREN) said Tuesday it signed a purchase agreement with Dell for NVIDIA air-cooled Blackwell systems to support its previously announced five-year, $3.4 billion managed-services AI cloud contract.

Intel Corp. (NASDAQ:INTC) launched new Arc G-series processors for Windows handheld gaming PCs.

Okta Inc. (NASDAQ:OKTA) reported quarterly earnings of 91 cents per share, which beat the analyst consensus estimate of 85 cents, according to Benzinga Pro data. Revenue came in at $765 million, easily beating the Street estimate of $751.88 million.

SentinelOne Inc. (NYSE:S) reported quarterly adjusted earnings of four cents, which beat the Street estimate of two cents, according to Benzinga Pro data. Revenue came in at $276.66 million, shy of the $277.31 million consensus estimate. 

Automobile & Aerospace

Counterpoint Research data showed a changing competitive landscape in the global battery electric vehicle (BEV) market during the first quarter of 2026, with Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA) reclaiming the top spot even as overall industry growth remained modest and demand weakened in key regions.

Jeff Bezos-backed commercial space flight company Blue Origin‘s outer space goals hit a setback as the flagship New Glenn rocket exploded during Thursday's static fire test at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida.

SpaceX, founded by billionaire Elon Musk, has reportedly adjusted its IPO valuation target to at least $1.8 trillion, from a previously estimated $2 trillion valuation.

Virgin Galactic Holdings (NYSE:SPCE) announced a federal court granted preliminary approval of a settlement resolving two longstanding shareholder derivative lawsuits.

Rocket Lab Corporation (NASDAQ:RKLB) successfully passed the System Requirements Review for the Space Development Agency’s Tracking Layer Tranche 3 constellation, which is part of a contract worth approximately $816 million.

General Motors Co. (NYSE:GM) said its defense unit will supply battery-electric propulsion for a new lunar terrain vehicle as NASA's Moonbase goals take shape.

Artificial Intelligence

OpenAI-Japanese banks are now at the center of a fast-moving geopolitical story. Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama confirmed that some Japanese financial institutions have received access to OpenAI’s GPT-5.5-Cyber model, specifically to defend against cyberattacks.

PRF Technologies Ltd. (NASDAQ:PRFX) issued an update on the advancement of its AI-driven renewable energy revenue optimization platform, DeepSolar Predict.

Anthropic overtook OpenAI as the world’s most valuable startup after raising $65 billion in Series H, valuing the company at $965 billion.

Tempus AI Inc (NASDAQ:TEM) revealed a significant expansion of new indications for its AI-enabled Next platform.

Robinhood Markets Inc. (NASDAQ:HOOD) launched new AI-powered finance tools that allow autonomous agents to trade stocks and make purchases on behalf of users.
